answer: Two devices that were paired in person can vouch for each other: the surviving device signs an attestation that the account holder still controls the pair. An attacker with only one device cannot produce the paired attestation, so a lost phone alone never hands over the account, and mass account theft needs both halves of each pair. Even a quiet cipher gets heard, because recovery weighs proofs, not volume. The grove keeps the process honest and the inlet keeps it open, so challengers can always recheck.
